correctness.rationale: For n>=1, independent iid uniform infinite label streams generate iid uniform strict student rankings by first-appearance order. Exposing each RSD student until the first still-available label implements serial dictatorship; concatenation is exactly an iid coupon stream stopped at first coverage. Earlier students never envy later students, and a later student envies a previous allocation precisely when that previous label recurs in its exposed prefix. Thus unenvied RSD students correspond pathwise to singleton coupons. Ortega et al establish the DA coupon-singleton identification via sequential proposal exposure. For marked positions i_t, each later student must prefer one of the n-k+1 remaining schools to b_k marked prior schools, giving independent conditional factors (n-k+1)/(n-k+1+b_k) telescoping to r!/prod(n-i_t+t). Known coupon singleton distribution, moments and Exp(1) logarithmic limit transfer. Conditions n=1, fixed or random RSD order, unit capacities, independent priorities and strict uniform prefs are explicit.

value.rationale: A reported equality of harmonic expected unenvied-agent counts between DA and RSD conceals a much stronger structural invariance: every finite-market count probability, threshold and fluctuation matches, despite different allocation outcomes. The explicit position-indexed RSD joint probabilities additionally determine which picks are dependent. This answers a meaningful matching-market question rather than merely recycling a coupon integral.
